import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/data/nls_raw.csv')

# Correct column names
gender_column = 'Sex of respondent, 1979'
degree_completion_column = 'Highest grade completed, 1979'

# Check if the columns exist
if gender_column in df.columns and degree_completion_column in df.columns:
    # Convert gender to categorical (1: Male, 2: Female)
    df[gender_column] = df[gender_column].astype(int)
    
    # Group by gender and calculate mean degree completion
    gender_groups = df.groupby(gender_column)[degree_completion_column].mean()
    
    # Perform t-test to check for statistical significance
    male_degrees = df[df[gender_column] == 1][degree_completion_column]
    female_degrees = df[df[gender_column] == 2][degree_completion_column]
    t_stat, p_value = ttest_ind(male_degrees, female_degrees)
    
    # Plot the distribution of degree completion by gender
    sns.histplot(data=df, x=degree_completion_column, hue=gender_column, kde=True)
    plt.title('Distribution of Degree Completion by Gender')
    plt.xlabel('Highest Grade Completed')
    plt.ylabel('Frequency')
    plt.show()
    
    # Print results
    print("Mean degree completion by gender:")
    print(gender_groups)
    print("T-statistic:", t_stat)
    print("P-value:", p_value)
else:
    print("Columns for gender or degree completion not found.")

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.stats import ttest_ind

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/data/nls_raw.csv')

# Correct column names
gender_column = 'Sex of respondent, 1979'
degree_completion_column = 'Highest grade completed, 1979'

# Check if the columns exist
if gender_column in df.columns and degree_completion_column in df.columns:
    # Drop rows with missing values in the relevant columns
    df_clean = df.dropna(subset=[gender_column, degree_completion_column])
    
    # Convert gender to categorical (1: Male, 2: Female)
    df_clean[gender_column] = df_clean[gender_column].astype(int)
    
    # Group by gender and calculate mean degree completion
    gender_groups = df_clean.groupby(gender_column)[degree_completion_column].mean()
    
    # Perform t-test to check for statistical significance
    male_degrees = df_clean[df_clean[gender_column] == 1][degree_completion_column]
    female_degrees = df_clean[df_clean[gender_column] == 2][degree_completion_column]
    t_stat, p_value = ttest_ind(male_degrees, female_degrees)
    
    # Plot the distribution of degree completion by gender
    sns.histplot(data=df_clean, x=degree_completion_column, hue=gender_column, kde=True)
    plt.title('Distribution of Degree Completion by Gender')
    plt.xlabel('Highest Grade Completed')
    plt.ylabel('Frequency')
    plt.show()
    
    # Print results
    print("Mean degree completion by gender:")
    print(gender_groups)
    print("T-statistic:", t_stat)
    print("P-value:", p_value)
else:
    print("Columns for gender or degree completion not found.")
